title: Pay Operations Memorandum — Detour Exclusion in Cartwise Shopper Batches Mileage Claims
content:
In a mileage dispute on a Cartwise Shopper Batches batch, the detour exclusion method decides how many of the miles driven beyond the tolerance-grown estimate count toward the paid route. It reads the violations recorded against that batch on the shopper's Cartwise Shopper Contractor Accounts record:

1. When **one or more wrong-address violations** are recorded against the batch, those miles are multiplied by the delivered orders (the batch's orders less the wrong-address violations, never below zero) divided by all orders, and **rounded down to a tenth of a mile**.
2. When **no wrong-address violation but one or more late-delivery violations** are recorded against the batch, those miles are **halved and rounded down to a whole mile**.
3. Otherwise **all of them count**.

## Input — judgement — output

| Wrong-address violations against the batch | Late-delivery violations against the batch | Miles beyond that count |
|---|---|---|
| One or more | Any | Miles times delivered orders over all orders, rounded down to 0.1 mile |
| None | One or more | Half the miles, rounded down to a whole mile |
| None | None | All the miles |

A wrong-address violation decides the method whether or not late-delivery violations are also recorded.

## Worked figures (hypothetical: 3.7 miles beyond the grown estimate, 3 orders)

- One wrong-address violation: 3.7 multiplied by 2, divided by 3, is 2.4667, rounded down to 2.4 miles.
- Three wrong-address violations: no order delivered, so 0.0 miles.
- No wrong-address violation, one late-delivery violation: 3.7 halved is 1.85, rounded down to 1 mile.
- Neither: 3.7 miles.
